body:
WHAT
A child session (a subagent) that was created with explicit numeric caps stops when it reaches settings.maxIterationsPerTurn tool rounds or when its own output tokens pass settings.maxTokensPerTurn. One round before the iteration cap it receives a reminder telling it this is the final tool round.

WHY
Without the cap a runaway subagent could loop forever; without the final-round warning a weak model is cut off mid-exploration with no final answer.

WHERE
engine/core/src/runtime/session.ts — Session.runTurn(): `const capped = this.opts.child ?? false`; the two `if (capped && …)` checks at the top of the for-loop (maxIterationsPerTurn → stopReason 'max_iterations', maxTokensPerTurn → break) and the `if (capped && iteration === this.settings.maxIterationsPerTurn - 2)` final-round this.remind(). Note Session.spawnAgent() sets childSettings.maxIterationsPerTurn/maxTokensPerTurn to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so a bound only bites for a child built directly with child:true and finite settings.

TEST CHECKLIST
1. A Session constructed with child:true and maxIterationsPerTurn:3, fed a FakeProvider that always returns a tool call, stops after exactly 3 provider requests and emits turn_finished with stopReason 'max_iterations'.
2. The same child session emits a command_output event whose text starts with '⏸ Iteration cap reached'.
3. With maxIterationsPerTurn:3 the user message sent on the request following round index 1 contains the reminder text 'Final tool round: the per-turn iteration cap is reached after this response'.
4. A child with maxTokensPerTurn:100 and FakeProvider turns reporting usage.outputTokens:80 each stops before the third model call and emits a '⏸ Turn token budget reached' command_output.
5. A root session (child:false) with the same tiny caps is NOT stopped by them: with 5 scripted tool-call turns followed by an end_turn, all 6 provider requests are made and no 'cap reached' message is emitted.
